first.rationale: The objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so the competitor's entry pricing is a trap rather than a brief: memory_73 records that promotional pricing does win price-sensitive SMB acquisition and revenue but materially damaged 30-day retention and explicitly carries a do-not-generalize caveat. Buying churning accounts in response to a price war spends the one slot on revenue that does not persist, so promotional_pricing is out despite being the most direct match to the competitive threat. Of the two measured declines, onboarding completion (-4%) is plausibly upstream of activation (-6%): memory_86 ties shortened onboarding to completion, time-to-value, and early adoption across self-serve, and memory_31 independently ties signup simplification to durable first-week activation lift. Two partially independent records pointing the same direction is the strongest inherited signal available, and fixing the upstream constraint may recover part of the activation gap as a side effect, whereas activation_messaging (memory_91) treats the downstream symptom only. I am verifying memory_86 because it is the load-bearing record for my chosen action and I want the original effect size, sample, and durability window rather than the consolidated summary; and memory_91 because it is the strongest alternative and if its week-one engagement lift is larger or better measured than memory_86's completion lift, I should switch. I am deliberately not spending budget on memory_73 — its caveat only needs to be directionally true to disqualify pricing, so verifying it cannot change my action. Downstream risk: stripping signup fields can degrade the qualification data that feeds the demo-request path memory_44 credits with superior enterprise pipeline quality, so the test must be scoped to self-serve SMB, leave the enterprise route untouched, and carry 30-day retention plus lead-quality guardrails, not just completion rate. Both supporting memories are archived summaries whose original conditions predate the current competitive environment; the prior lifts were measured without a price-aggressive competitor present, so effect sizes may not transfer even if direction does. Standard experiment scale, not broad rollout, for that reason. If verification shows memory_86 rests on a thin or short-horizon record, I fall back to activation_messaging, which addresses the larger decline and carries no known retention harm.

final.rationale: Verification overturned my intended action, so I am switching. The consolidated memory_86 said only that shortened onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value; the source record shows 60-day churn +9% concentrated in complex-workspace accounts and an explicit do-not-roll-out instruction for that segment. The summary had silently dropped the harm and the scope limit. Since I cannot cleanly separate simple from complex workspaces in a one-week slot under competitive pressure, and since retained accounts are exactly what 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue' means, simplify_onboarding is off the table. memory_91 verified clean and strong: week-one engagement +11%, activation +6%, 30-day retention +1%. It is the only candidate with a verified positive retention signal, and it targets the larger of the two declines (-6% activation) directly. Promotional_pricing remains disqualified by memory_73's retention damage — it would buy churning accounts in a price war. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) does not address either measured decline. Referral_incentive (memory_57) is plausible and retention-neutral but addresses neither symptom and depends on an established-customer base rather than the acquisition and activation gap in front of me. The most important carry-forward is not the action but the failure mode: consolidation stripped a material caveat from memory_86 while preserving one in memory_73, which means the inherited layer is not uniformly trustworthy and unverified summaries cannot be treated as complete. memory_31 (signup simplification) is now specifically suspect — it is adjacent to the record that proved lossy, was never verified, and may carry a similar hidden segment-specific harm; it should not be acted on until pulled. I am also re-flagging memory_57 as unverified. Downstream risk on the chosen action: in-product messaging that pushes accounts toward a 'first meaningful action' can inflate a shallow activation metric without real value delivery, and heavier nudging risks annoyance in accounts already struggling with onboarding completion (-4%, still unaddressed and likely a real upstream constraint). So I am running this as a standard experiment, not a broad rollout, with 30-day retention and downstream qualified-revenue guardrails rather than activation rate alone. exp_91's conditions also predate the current competitor's entry pricing, so the +6% may not transfer at full size even though direction is well supported. If activation recovers but onboarding completion keeps sliding, the correct next slot is a segmented onboarding test that respects the complex-workspace boundary exp_86 identified — not a repeat of the flow that produced the churn.
